court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm statutory authority to review the BIA’s denial of reopening.

issues.label: Final order reviewability
issues.why: Court must determine whether the challenged BIA decision is a final, reviewable order.

issues.label: Scope of review
issues.why: Court must delineate what parts of the IJ/BIA reasoning and record are properly before it.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply correct standards (abuse of discretion for reopening; de novo for legal questions; substantial evidence for factual determinations).

issues.label: Exhaustion of issues
issues.why: Court must ensure the arguments raised were presented to the agency or are otherwise exempt from exhaustion.

issues.label: Waiver/forfeiture
issues.why: Court must decide whether any arguments were waived by inadequate briefing or forfeited below.

issues.label: Separate petition interaction
issues.why: Court must account for overlap or preclusion issues with Petition No. 24-7433.

issues.label: Timeliness of motion
issues.why: Court must confirm the motion was properly treated as timely via equitable tolling.

issues.label: Equitable tolling standard
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether ineffective assistance and diligence satisfy tolling requirements.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance compliance
issues.why: Court must check procedural prerequisites for IAC claims (e.g., Lozada-type requirements) and prejudice where relevant.

issues.label: Reopening regulatory requirements
issues.why: Court must ensure the motion met required contents (evidence, affidavits, and arguments) under reopening rules.

issues.label: New or previously unavailable evidence
issues.why: Court must decide whether submitted materials qualify as new/unavailable evidence rather than cumulative information.

issues.label: Changed country conditions
issues.why: Court must consider whether evidence shows materially changed conditions since the prior hearing/decision.

issues.label: Proper comparison baseline
issues.why: Court must determine whether the BIA compared new evidence to conditions at the correct time (hearing vs prior decision).

issues.label: Continuation vs change
issues.why: Court must assess whether the BIA wrongly rejected evidence as “continuation” despite new severity, scope, or documentation.

issues.label: Materiality to CAT claim
issues.why: Court must determine whether the new evidence is material to the likelihood-of-torture inquiry.

issues.label: Prima facie CAT eligibility
issues.why: Court must ensure the BIA applied the correct “reasonable likelihood”/prima facie standard for reopening.

issues.label: Likelihood standard clarity
issues.why: Court must check whether the BIA improperly demanded proof meeting the ultimate “more likely than not” merits standard at reopening.

issues.label: Detention likelihood finding
issues.why: Court must assess the legal/factual sufficiency of the BIA’s finding that Parada may be detained under the State of Exception.

issues.label: Torture definition application
issues.why: Court must confirm the BIA used the correct legal definition of “torture” (severity, intent, purpose).

issues.label: Specific intent requirement
issues.why: Court must address whether prison conditions and abuses described satisfy CAT’s specific-intent component.

issues.label: Lawful sanctions exception
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether harms are improperly treated as lawful sanctions rather than torture/ill-treatment.

issues.label: Acquiescence standard
issues.why: Court must apply the correct test for government involvement or acquiescence (including willful blindness).

issues.label: State actor involvement
issues.why: Court must consider whether alleged abuse is by police/military/prison officials or with their consent.

issues.label: Particularized risk analysis
issues.why: Court must ensure the BIA assessed Parada’s individualized risk, not only generalized country conditions.

issues.label: Group-based risk relevance
issues.why: Court must decide how evidence about deportees/suspected gang members applies to Parada’s characteristics.

issues.label: Aggregation of risk sources
issues.why: Court must consider combined risks from detention, prison abuse, and other actors cumulatively.

issues.label: Country-conditions evidence treatment
issues.why: Court must determine whether the BIA properly considered relevant reports, articles, and expert submissions.

issues.label: Improper quantitative-evidence rule
issues.why: Court must decide whether the BIA committed legal error by requiring “quantitative evidence” for CAT claims.

issues.label: Anecdotal evidence admissibility
issues.why: Court must address whether credible qualitative accounts can establish likelihood of torture under CAT.

issues.label: Expert report weight
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether the BIA gave a reasoned explanation for discounting expert testimony.

issues.label: Reasoned decisionmaking
issues.why: Court must assess whether the BIA adequately explained its conclusions and addressed key evidence.

issues.label: Selective evidence consideration
issues.why: Court must determine whether the BIA impermissibly ignored or mischaracterized probative evidence.

issues.label: Record-based decisionmaking
issues.why: Court must ensure the BIA relied on the administrative record and permissible inferences, not speculation.

issues.label: Internal inconsistency
issues.why: Court must check for inconsistency between acknowledging detention risk and rejecting torture likelihood without adequate rationale.

issues.label: Probability assessment method
issues.why: Court must assess whether the BIA used a lawful approach to probability (not requiring statistical certainty).

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: Court must ensure burdens were properly placed on Parada for reopening and CAT eligibility.

issues.label: Presumption or evidentiary bars
issues.why: Court must verify no improper presumptions (e.g., against detainees/deportees) skewed the CAT analysis.

issues.label: Due process in reopening
issues.why: Court must consider whether the BIA’s evidentiary demands or refusals denied a fundamentally fair hearing.

issues.label: Prejudice from legal error
issues.why: Court must determine whether any legal error (e.g., quantitative requirement) was harmless or warrants remand.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy
issues.why: Court must decide whether to grant the petition and remand to the BIA, and with what instructions.

issues.label: Remand scope limitations
issues.why: Court must specify whether remand permits additional fact-finding or requires application of correct legal standards only.
